**International Copper Study Group Environmental and Economic Committee Twenty Seventh Regular Meeting 6 October 2009, 10.45 am – 1.00 pm Lisbon, Portugal** 

**ICSG/EEC27/7** 

### **Report on Progress in the 2009/2010 Environmental and Economic Committee Work Program** 

The Environmental and Economic Committee was created to discuss and promote actions relevant to environmental and economic issues affecting the copper industry and market.  In order to fulfill this mandate, the Committee has produced a series of publications on environmental regulations, recycling, first use capacities and other topics. 

Brief descriptions of current activities for each EEC approved work program item are provided below, together with a table giving an Overview of the EEC Regular Work Program and Projects and Initiatives. Two new project proposals are also outlined. 

### **Current Regular Activities** 

– <u>Directory of First Use Capacities (Item E1)</u> The directory provides a systematic global overview of companies and plants involved in the “first use” of copper - the use of unwrought copper materials (refined copper, alloy ingots, direct melt scrap, etc.) as feed to the production of semi-fabricated products (copper wire rod; copper and copper alloy, sheet, strip, bar, rod, tube, etc.). It covers wire-rod plants, brass mills and electrodeposited copper foil mills. It also covers ingot makers and master alloy plants as suppliers to foundries and brass mills. The 2009 edition of the Directory was published in March 2009 and the results were presented at the April 2009 ICSG meeting. The next ICSG Directory of First Use will be published in late 2010 (utilising input from Project P17). 

<u>Annual Recyclables Survey (Item E2)</u> The ICSG conducts an annual survey of global copper scrap use focused on secondary refined production and copper content of directly melted copper and copper alloy scrap for the production of semis, casting ingots, and castings. The results are published annually. The 2009 report was published in April 2009 with the results presented at the April 2009 Meeting. The 2010 edition is scheduled for publication in Spring 2010. 

<u><mark>Survey of Regulations (Item E3)</mark></u> <mark>This annual survey maps out national regulations, legislation and conventions affecting copper products in different countries and identifies the sectors, sub-sectors and when possible, copper commodities potentially affected. The secretariat provided members with an updated document at the October 2008 ICSG meeting (Changes in the Regulatory Environment for Copper in 2008 ICSG/EEC/25/4).  This report covered changes in regulations affecting copper for the period October 2007 to October 2008 and identified international agreements related to climate change and probable impacts on energy generation and compliance costs, advances in the design of new EU energy and climate change regulations, the implementation of chemical control legislation (REACH) and chang

es in the EU Drinking Water Directive. The survey included United States Senate Bill 2006 restricting activities of scrap metal traders, advances on the regulations for mining contract renegotiations in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the decree raising China selling price of electricity, coke coal and aluminum new export tariffs in China, strengthened controls on inflows of foreign exchange, China import prohibition of copper related wastes, and the approved recycling law effective in 2009. New Indonesian mining legislation and smelting capacity impacts was included, and also the draft law in Chile creating a Ministry of the Environment and an Environmental Enforcement Superintendent’s Office. Advances of the Draft for the new mining law for Kazakhstan are included, and the new mining law and tax regime recently introduced in Zambia. Western Australia’s new mine closure and</mark> 

<mark>rehabilitation system is summarized, followed by provincial legislation affecting copper/gold investments in Argentina, and advances in the new draft mining regulations in Ecuador. Recent and expected regulatory developments will be presented in October 2009 with the launching of the 2009 Edition of ICSG Survey of Regulations Affecting Copper Products (ICSG/EEC27/2).</mark> 

<u>Monitoring & Reporting on International Issues (Item E4)</u> ICSG monitors and reports on international issues which may affect copper, including the work conducted by other international organizations, and briefs member countries when issues come forward. The main current issues of interest include the international economy, sustainable development, energy, the environment, and trade. Analyses have been conducted on topics including refined copper usage and the world economy, production and trade of semi-fabricated copper and copper alloy products, secondary copper production, and copper price volatility. Recently, ICSG funded the translation of the COCHILCO Report on Best Practices and Efficient Use of Water in the Mining Industry in June 2009 and a new Insight piece on the impacts of the ongoing economic crisis on the copper industry was published in September 2009. 

### **Current Project Activities** 

<u>Recycling Rates Project/Copper Flow Model (Item P10)</u> The ICSG secretariat developed the Copper Flow Model (CFM) as a key tool for understanding copper flows in a particular country and determining the efficiency of recycling of copper from end-of-life products. It was applied by the secretariat for Western Europe, the USA and, most recently, Brazil. An assessment of ICSG copper flow model applications was included in the interim report of the copper scrap project in 2008. As part of the study on the Copper Scrap Market in Japan and International Trade of Copper Scrap being prepared for ICSG, the Metal Economic Research Institute of Japan (MERI/J) will produce an update of the CFM for Japan. In addition, improved data generated by the study on Global Recycled Copper Use

in Copper/Alloy Semis Manufacturers in the Rest of the World being conducted by Nathan Associates for ICSG Copper Scrap Project will include a basic global copper flow model based on the standard ICSG methodology and calibrated with the latest data from the ICSG Copper Bulletin. In an industry that is clearly globalised the development of a more global analysis of the copper flows is required instead of national models. Estimations of copper content and recovery rates by country for the following end of life products would be required: waste electric and electronic equipment, end of life vehicles, construction waste, industrial electrical equipment waste, industrial non-electrical equipment waste and municipal solid waste. Estimations of total copper use by country including scrap use and net semis trade, and copper content in the net international trade flows, are also needed. The secretariat will look at developing possible project proposals in this area for consideration at the April 2010 ICSG meeting. 

<u>Country/Sector Profiles (P11)</u> Information is collected in a comprehensive and systematic manner providing regular views of the economic, market and trade performance of countries and companies involved in copper markets. Profiles have been completed for Indonesia, India, Brazil and Zambia. A draft country profile for the DR Congo was presented at the October 2008 meeting and is being revised subject to the completion of the mining contract negotiations in the DRC. Potential country profile candidates previously identified include South Korea and Peru. 

<u>Copper Scrap Project (Item P12)</u> This project was initiated by the Study Group in 2007. The scope and focus of the project has been discussed and revised at subsequent meetings. At the April 2009 meeting, member country representatives were presented with recent project 

advances and proposed final steps. The Committee also approved the proposed reallocation of 4,000 Euros to undertake research on trends in the generation of domestic copper scrap in China and the secretariat request to sell the India and China copper scrap market reports. A workshop on Policy and Incentives for Copper Scrap Trade, Recycling and Use will be held at the October 2009 EEC Meeting. In addition, member country representatives will be presented with research findings from ICSG-commissioned reports from MERI/J on the Japan Copper Scrap Market, from BGRIMM on Chinese Smelters and Semis Scrap Use Survey and Domestic Copper Scrap Generation in China, and from Nathan Associates on Copper Scrap Use in the Rest of the World. The secretariat will also present the Committee with the latest research and preparation for the draft final report to be presented in April 2010 (ICSG/EEC27/3). 

<u>CFC Projects (Item P15)</u> The Study Group, as an officially recognized International Commodity Body by the Common Fund for Commodities, serves as a supervisory body in a series of copper-relevant CFC projects (approved, sub

mitted, or in preparation) intended to promote the economic utilisation of copper. Members will be briefed on current projects and recent proposals at the October 2009 Meeting. 

<u>Constraints on New Copper Supply Coming On Stream (Item P16) In 2008 April Meeting</u> member country representatives agreed that a study on “Constraints on New Copper Supply Coming On Stream” be investigated.  The Secretariat presented a document with updated data of different supply constraints observed in 2007 and 2008 (documents ICSG/EEC25/3 and ICSG Constraints Annex) and presented a project proposal approved at the October 2008 ICSG meeting. Members agreed that the project should not focus on cost analysis but should look at investment regimes, financial, geological and other decision-making factors that determine whether a project is developed, and funding was granted in the amount of €8,000. The secretariat presented information and analysis on recent developments affecting 2009-2012 copper supply at the April 2009 meeting, including analysis of the impact of higher capital costs on the copper projects pipeline, feasibility study biases and predictable mistakes in the economic feasibility studies, bibliographic research on the impact of strikes and market power. A summary of contents of COCHILCO Report on Good Practices and Efficient Use of Water in the Mining Industry, competitiveness and trends in key copper mining inputs, and long term trends for copper production was also presented. 

Member countries requested additional research on the impact of mining taxes and investment regimes on future copper supply, and approved the allocation of 5,000 Euros for an external study on the topic. Mr James Otto, Attorney and Mineral Economist, was contracted to conduct the study and delivered the final report in late August 2009: Framework for Analyzing the Impacts of Investment Legislation and Tax Regimes on Global Copper Supply Coming on Stream. The study found that geological endowment was the main driver of copper mine investments included in ICSG Directory of Copper Mines and Plants in the past, and recommended a follow up survey to identify potential supply constraints that may deter or delay known up coming copper mine projects going ahead on schedule. The secretariat has prepared a final report of this research project, including a summary of the contracted study and secretariat research, and will present its findings at the October 2009 meeting (ICSG/EEC27/6). 

### <u>China Copper Semis Capacity Database (P17)</u> 

At the April 2009 EEC meetings ember country representatives approved the secretariat proposal to hire a consulting firm in China to improve the data on the capacity and production of Chinese copper and copper alloy semis plants, and approved the funding request in the amount of 15,000 Euros. The purpose of the project is to improve the ICSG profile of the current copper and copper alloy semis production capacity in China, the world’s largest 

pr

oducer, with new large plants and new capacity coming in the 2010-2012 pipeline. All fabricators in the database will be first copper usage plants: wire rod mills, tube mills (ACR tube, normal copper tube and alloy tube mills), sheet/strip mills (Copper and copper alloy sheet/strip) non-electrical rod mills (mechanical copper rod, brass rod, copper alloy rod), nonelectrical wire mill (non-electrical copper wire and copper alloy wire) and large foundries only. The project will enable ICSG to follow the situation of overcapacity by type of product. New programs, including both under construction and probable projects within next 3 years, will be summarized. Contacts with authorities and professionals of Chinese industry associations, research centers and other institutions will be also carried out. If necessary, local authorities will be contacted. The project will transform the current Directory database on capacity of Chinese copper and copper alloy semis plants into a database with direct contacts in the plant, eliminating plants closed and allowing more direct interaction between ICSG secretariat and the plants in the future. BGRIMM has been contracted to conduct the work with the first report due April 2010 and the final report due by October 2010. ### **New Proposals** Copper End Use Agreement with ICA The secretariat will present to member countries a proposal for a project in cooperation with the International Copper Association (ICA) on the collection, analysis and dissemination of copper end use data. Member countries will be invited to consider and discuss the project, seek clarification of any issues that might be unclear, and if there is consensus give approval for the project to proceed (subject to the negotiation by the secretariat of appropriate contractual arrangements with ICA) (ICSG/EEC27/4). Index of Leading Economic Indicators The secretariat proposed to members at the April 2009 meeting that the creation of an Index of Leading Indicators of Copper Usage be examined. Following the member country representative suggestion to examine other leading indicators currently being produced, including the Copper Index published by the US Geological Survey, the secretariat has conducted research on constructing such an index. The research findings and a proposal to create a new ICSG Index of Leading Economic Indicators project will be presented to member country representatives at the October 2009 EEC Meeting (ICSG/EEC27/5). ### **Action for Member Countries** Delegates are invited to consider the reports on current and proposed new work items, to give approvals if appropriate, and to suggest additions or deletions. **International Copper Study Group Environmental and Economic Committee Twenty Seventh Regular Meeting 6 October 2009, 10.45 am – 1.00 pm Lisbon, Portugal** ## **ICSG/EEC27/7** # **ENVIRONMENTAL AND ECONOMIC COMMITTEE WORK PROGRAM** ||||**Fund Allocated (€) as**||**2008**
